newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek money rates sit idle in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek money rates sit idle in late trade.

text.p: Greek interbank rates were fluctuating narrowly around morning levels with tomnext hitting 13.40 percent in intraday dealing as liquidity concerns continued to haunt the market, traders said.
"Rates are little changed since this morning with tomnext at 13.40 percent," said a dealer at a state bank. "Liquidity concerns are behind the rate pick up ahead of tomorrow's T-bill sales."

The finance ministry will issue three-, six- and 12-month T-bills on October 31 at 12.30 percent, 11.70 percent and 11.50 percent respectively, down from 12.70 percent, 12.10 percent and 11.90 percent at end-September.
Other dealers said they expected overnight funds to open around 13.40 percent in anticipation of a liquidity squeeze from bouyant sales of T-bills on Thursday.
The mark was quoted at 157.00/10 drachmas from Wednesday's 157.130 fix, the dollar at 236.88/93 drachmas from 237.560 and the Ecu at 300.79/89 from 301.250 drachmas.
"There was little action at the fixing and the central bank drove ecu/drachma higher," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
